human: We theoretically investigate Cooper quartet correlations in doubly-magic nuclei( Ca 40 , Sn 100 , and Pb 164 ).We first examine the quartet condensation fraction in infinite symmetric nuclear matter by using the quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory.Together with the total nucleon density profiles of doubly-magic nuclei obtained from the Skyrme Hartree-Fock calculation,we discuss the spatial distribution of quartet correlations in finite nuclei within the local density approximation.Large quartet condensate fractions are found at the surface region of an atomic nucleus due to the strong neutron-proton attractive interactions responsible for the deuteron formation in vacuum.Moreover, we discuss a possible microscopic origin of the Wigner term in the context of nucleon-quartet scattering in dilute symmetric nuclear matter.The nucleon-quartet scattering effect on the Wigner term is numerically estimated as about one order of magnitude of the total empirical strength,indicating the importance of multi-nucleon clusters in the symmetry energy and mass formula in addition to the neutron-proton pairing.
ai: In our theoretical exploration, we delve into the realm of Cooper quartet correlations specifically within doubly-magic nuclei, namely ^40Ca, ^100Sn, and ^164Pb. Initially, we focus on scrutinizing the condensation fraction of quartets within an infinite expanse of symmetric nuclear matter, employing the quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer BCS theory. Coupled with total nucleon density profiles derived from the Skyrme Hartree-Fock method applicable to doubly-magic nuclei, we embark on analyzing the spatial arrangement of quartet correlations present in finite nuclei, leveraging the local density approximation. Significant fractions of quartet condensates manifest predominantly at the nuclear surface. This is a consequence of the potent neutron-proton attraction forces which also facilitate the formation of deuterons in a vacuum environment. Furthermore, we explore a possible microscopic origin of the Wigner term through the lens of nucleon-quartet interactions within a dilute, symmetric nuclear matter framework. The impact of nucleon-quartet scattering on the Wigner term is rigorously quantified and estimated to be approximately tenfold of the total empirical strength. This highlights and underscores the crucial role played by multi-nucleon clusters in influencing both the symmetry energy and the nuclear mass formula. These effects go beyond mere neutron-proton pair interactions, implicating the necessity of considering quartet dynamics in comprehensive nuclear models.

In addition to this, the BCS theory has been expanded to include quartet correlations, giving rise to the quartet BCS QBCS theory, which has found applications in analyzing nuclei [20, 21] as well as nuclear matter [22, 23]. Although the QBCS theory, based on the quartet coherent state, does not preserve particle-number conservation even within finite nuclei, the correlation energy outcomes are strikingly consistent with those from the QCM, which does uphold particle-number conservation [20]. Therefore, QBCS theory emerges as a promising framework for depicting Cooper quartet correlations, even within finite nuclei. Nevertheless, the spatial distribution of quartet correlations in mediumor heavy-mass nuclei remains somewhat ambiguous due to computational complexities hindering clear insights.
